 Order

This misc. appeal u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by appellants-claimants seeking enhancement of compensation amount by taking exception to the Award dated 09/07/2009 passed by Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to the Court of First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.62/2009,
whereby the Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,14,500/- along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization in favour of claimants on account of death of Wahid Khan in a motor accident.
2.The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. Challenging the impugned Award, it is contended on behalf of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:240 2 MA-1038-2009 appellants/claimants that the deceased was the owner of a truck bearing registration No. MP06/E/6307 and was holding a valid licence to drive heavy motor vehicles.
Hence, the deceased was a skilled labourer.
However, the Claims Tribunal has erroneously assessed the income of the deceased at Rs. 2,500/- per month, which is on the lower side and wholly unrealistic.

It is further submitted that, considering the nature of work and ownership of the vehicle,
the Claims Tribunal ought to have assessed the income of the deceased at Rs. 20,000/- per month.
Smt.Nargis vs Jhirmal Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58482925/
1 Therefore, it is prayed that a reasonable and just amount of compensation be awarded to the claimants by enhancing the impugned Award.
Accordingly, it is prayed that the impugned Award be set aside and a just and reasonable amount of compensation be awarded in favour of the claimants.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and prayed for dismissal of appeal.
5. Having heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award as well as record of Claims Tribunal.
6. It is undisputed that deceased was driver of the heavy vehicle, therefore, he was skilled labour.
7. From a perusal of the record, it is evident that the deceased was the owner of a truck bearing registration No. MP06/E/6307.
From a perusal of the passbook (Ex. P/12), it is clear that the same pertains to a Public Provident Fund scheme, wherein deposits were made regularly even after the death of the deceased.
However, no cogent or substantial evidence has been adduced by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:240 3 MA-1038-2009 claimants to establish the actual income of the deceased.
From the evidence on record, it is apparent that the deceased was the owner of the offending truck and was holding a valid licence to drive a heavy motor vehicle.

Therefore, in the absence of documentary proof regarding income, the income of the deceased is required to be assessed on the basis of the prevailing minimum wages as on the date of the accident,
which is Rs. 5,500/- per month.

8. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 40% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.

9. Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUN  Income Rs.5500 X 12= 660  After adding Future Prospects@40% Rs.26,400/-
 After adding Dependency 3/4 Rs.69,300/-
 Loss of Income Rs.69,300 X 17=11  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 6= 2  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
 Total Compensation =

2  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:240  4  11.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.14,48,100/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.4,14,500/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.10,33,600/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
12. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.10,33,600/- .
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

13. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants-claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
14. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
